title: Blitzortung Strike Daily Event Volume
dataSources: Seismograph (`seismo:reading`), Geiger counter (`geiger:cpm`), lightning strikes (`lightning:strike`), radon (`radon:reading`), all-sky meteor camera (`allsky:capture`), river-level gauge (`riverlevel:reading`), magnetometer (`magnetometer:reading`), satellite passes (`satpass:prediction`).
app: DIY citizen-science sensors — Raspberry Shake seismograph, Geiger counter, AS3935/Blitzortung lightning detector, radon monitor, all-sky meteor camera, river-level gauge, and magnetometer — via MQTT and scripted inputs to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=blitzortung:strike
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count as events, dc(station_id) as distinct_entities by _time
| sort - _time
description: Counts how many Blitzortung strike events land each day and how many distinct station values are represented.
value: Daily volume is the fastest way to spot a dead feed, a sudden burst, or a workflow that quietly changed.
implementation: Ingest Blitzortung strike records into `index=personal`; schedule daily and compare count and distinct station values against your normal baseline.
visualization: Column chart of daily event count with a line for distinct entities.
grandmaExplanation: It estimates how much Blitzortung strike activity showed up each day so you can see if the feed went quiet or suddenly got busy.
